questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It's not our book; it must be__ theres__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Theirs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **possessive pronouns** include '**yours, your, my, mine, our, ours, its, his, her, hers, their, theirs '__**. These are all words that demonstrate **ownership.**
 
• **Theirs **is a possessive pronoun.
 
• So, the correct answer is **option 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• ** **The idea that theirs needs an apostrophe comes out of the fact that every other word with, ‘s indicates possession, so English speakers sometimes think theirs should be spelled their’s. However, this is always incorrect – theirs is the only correct spelling.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. **

A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India __have increased 50 times__ over the last three years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e., Has increased 50 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a9d568b6419aa6ff37bbc42d94c53d413184d6cf8d7840be45cac8c3a302863.png] **Let's look at the following points-**

__
 
• The sentence uses the incorrect plural verb '**have increased**'.
 
• The subject of the verb is the singular '**use**'.
 
• ** Important Point: **
 
• ** Subject Verb Agreement Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb; while a plural subject requires a plural verb. *Example: She talks. (Singular); They talk. (Plural).***
 
• Here, the singular subject '**Use**' requires the singular present perfect verb '**Has increased**'.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d407e393fc273aca07f0a376b0337bc9a3bd769df6ce218173eeb8b6ab61fd95.png] Confusion Point-**

 
• Option 3, '**has been increased to 50 times'** is grammatically correct; but using 'To' requires a comparative noun in order to be meaningful. (Increased to 50 times of what?)
 
• So, in order to be correct, the structure would be: Increased to 50 times (of) the original value. 

**Thus, the rectified sentence is:** *A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India **has increased 50 times__** over the last three years.*

• Reflexive pronouns are words like myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves and themselves.
 
• They refer back to a person or thing.

The given sentence is grammatically correct. So, no substitutions are needed.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We should also learn __to trust what he says__. After all, he is a reformed person now.

options.text: to give someone the benefit of the doubt
to wrap our head around something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'

 

Key Points:

 

In the sentence, the speaker suggests they should trust a person who has reformed, implying giving them chance despite doubts that may exist due to past behavior.

Example: Although he made mistakes in the past, we should trust him now as he is a reformed individual.

'To give someone the benefit of the doubt' is an idiom that closely mirrors this sentiment.

Example: I didn't agree with her decision, but I gave her the benefit of the doubt because she's usually right.

Additional Information:

 

'To make matters worse' (Option 2) refers to exacerbating a problem or situation.

'No pain, no gain' (Option 3) refers to needing to work hard (experiencing 'pain') to get results (the 'gain').

'To wrap our head around something' (Option 4) means trying to understand a complex concept or issue.

questions.question:

She had finished all her homework __from 5 a.m. on that day.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence: **"She had finished all her homework from 5 a.m. on that day,"** is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The preposition "from" is incorrect in this context. The correct preposition is **"by"** to indicate completion before a certain time.
 
• The correct phrase should be "by 5 a.m. on that day," **ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.**
 
• Thus, the error is located in the** preposition** and **the phrase **that follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She had finished all her homework **by 5 a.m. on that day**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "by 5 a.m. in that day" – The preposition "in" is incorrect in this context. It should be "on."
 
• **Option 2:** "No improvement" – This is incorrect as the original sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "till 5 a.m. at that day" – The prepositions "till" and "at" are incorrect in this context. It should be "by" and "on."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence.

Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, __contributing to sustainable population growth__ and a healthier society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. promoting a viable population increase .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence emphasizes the role of family planning programs in sustainable population growth.
 
• Option 1,** "promoting a viable population increase,"** maintains the idea of sustainability and growth, which aligns with the original meaning.
 
• Options 2, 3, and 4 introduce negativity or excessiveness (discouraging, explosion, unbalanced growth) that is not intended in the original context.

Correct sentence: *Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, contributing to promoting a viable population increase and a healthier society*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Family planning programs are typically associated with sustainable and controlled population growth, which is reflected in option 1.
 
• Ensuring a viable population increase implies growth that is manageable and beneficial to the society in the long term.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution required.

I sometimes pass a delivery man wheeling a large handcart of Japanese food. The card bears a striking message:

**__‘Creating a world where everyone believes in his own authenticity.’__**

options.text: Been created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity
Created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity
Creating a world whereas everyone believes in their own authenticity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "No Substitution Required". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The underlined segment correctly uses the present participle **"Creating" **to indicate an ongoing process or aim, which aligns with the message intended to convey an aspiration or vision.
 
• The use of **"everyone" **followed by **"in his own authenticity" **is traditionally correct but may not align with contemporary preferences for gender-neutral language.
 
• However, the focus of this question is on the clause structure rather than pronoun choice.
 
• Option 1 ("Been created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity") alters the tense inappropriately and lacks the auxiliary verb necessary for the passive voice, rendering it grammatically incorrect.
 
• Option 2 ("Created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity") changes the tense and removes the aspect of ongoing action or aspiration, which alters the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• Option 3 ("Creating a world whereas everyone believes in their own authenticity") introduces "whereas," which is incorrect because "whereas" is typically used to contrast two statements, not to introduce the content of a vision or goal.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4". **

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Give the cake to __which __asks for it first.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Whoever**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"whomever"** is used as an object pronoun in a sentence. It refers to "whoever" in situations where it is the object of the verb or preposition. (जिसको भी)

 
 
• **Example:** You can give the prize to whomever you like.
 
 
 
• The word **"whoever"** is a subject pronoun and is used to mean "any person who." It functions as the subject of the verb in the sentence. (जो कोई भी)
 
 
• **Example:** Whoever finishes the race first will win a prize.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "Give the cake to which asks for it first," the word "whoever" correctly substitutes "which" because the subject of the sentence needs a pronoun that refers to "any person who."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Whoever**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Whomever** (जिसको भी): Used when referring to the object of a sentence or clause.

 
 
• **Example:** She will help whomever needs assistance.
 
 
 
• **Whomsoever** (जिस किसी को भी): A formal version of "whomever," used to refer to the object in a sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** The award will be given to whomsoever the committee chooses.
 
 
 
• **Whichever** (जो भी): Refers to one or a few options from a group.
 
 
• **Example:** You can pick whichever dress you like for the party.
